request: Allow people to write their own corrections and validate without a mandatory plan match. Measure actual editing and validation, not only page opening.

plan_and_execution.step: Inspect screenshot failure and plan editing flows in all three deployed source versions
plan_and_execution.result: Direct editing must preserve the literal requested OF 266303; accepting a proposed plan entry 265958 does not satisfy the request.

plan_and_execution.step: Separate human edits from optional catalogue comparison
plan_and_execution.result: Pencil opens direct editing; plan lookup is a separate optional action. Written values, blanks and formatting survive subsequent comparisons.

plan_and_execution.step: Remove plan computation from save and validation
plan_and_execution.result: Writes atomically update human evidence and affected local derived fields. Validation flushes pending writes and makes one transition without running the matching engine.

plan_and_execution.step: Keep exports and history faithful to human corrections
plan_and_execution.result: Raw written values are archived. Parseable numbers retain numeric export types; arbitrary text remains available. A written date that cannot serve as a SQL date is preserved while a separate capture date indexes history.

plan_and_execution.step: Test race conditions and actual browser interaction
plan_and_execution.result: Disposable databases cover exact OF, intentional blanks, free text, stale revisions, delayed responses, failed save and retry, remove and undo, mobile width, single validation and exported facts.

plan_and_execution.step: Publish verified source with rollback and passive observation
plan_and_execution.result: Each app has a separate source baseline, guarded runtime manifest, same-host code/database backup, health verification, and persistent latency watcher.

measurement_contract.http: Full request duration, status, request id and action; starts also reveal requests that have not finished.
measurement_contract.browser: Edit submission through saved UI, or validation click through next-page rendering. Reported separately from HTTP.
measurement_contract.sampling: Exclude explicit X-OCR-Probe synthetic requests. Do not store form values, names or query strings. HTTP requests may include automated consumers and are not unique people.
measurement_contract.statistics: 15 minute, 1 hour and 24 hour windows expose counts, median, maximum, errors and slow actions. P95 requires at least 20 observations.

watcher.alert_destination: server journal; no email or external messages configured

measurement_contract.limitation: No observed real edits or validations after publication means performance in actual user traffic is not yet confirmed. Controlled browser tests are labelled separately.

research.method: Seven targeted searches (35 results) followed by eight primary-source documents. Existing implementation and production logs were checked before applying recommendations.

sources.finding: Blocking I/O inside async routes occupies the event loop; ordinary def routes can run through the thread pool.
sources.decision: Original synchronous edit and validation routes now run outside the event loop; async row writes offload database work. Concurrency regression test verifies another request can respond while a write is deliberately stalled.

sources.finding: Synchronous endpoints and background tasks share a bounded thread pool.
sources.decision: Remove avoidable computation and isolate CPU work rather than blindly raising thread limits or app worker count.

sources.finding: WAL allows readers alongside a writer, while SQLite still serializes writers.
sources.decision: Keep write transactions short and preserve CAS revision checks; do not hold a transaction while scoring a plan. WAL already exists in the deployed design.

sources.finding: Pools reuse connections and need bounded capacity and observable wait behavior.
sources.decision: Existing pooling is retained. Save and manual validation no longer need to load the planning catalogue. Existing PG duration/query/connection measurements remain available.

sources.finding: Query statistics distinguish expensive queries from repeated queries.
sources.decision: Use query evidence before proposing indexes or capacity changes; no speculative production extension or DDL was installed.

sources.finding: Visible interaction latency includes event processing and rendering, beyond an HTTP response.
sources.decision: Add separate browser interaction measurements ending after UI application and animation frames; do not call backend duration end-to-end user latency.

sources.finding: Navigation lifecycle has separate network and document phases.
sources.decision: Carry validation start across navigation using sessionStorage and finish when the destination renders.

sources.finding: HTTP duration metrics should use bounded operation labels and suitable units.
sources.decision: Use a small fixed action vocabulary, explicit milliseconds, separate failures, and no user or sheet identifiers in stored metric series.

remaining_performance_work.item: Observe real post-publication editing and validation with enough samples, especially queued saves and page navigation.
remaining_performance_work.trigger: Any error, incomplete write, or edit/validation exceeding two seconds emits a server watcher alert.

remaining_performance_work.item: CPIS exports still take approximately nine seconds in current production traffic.
remaining_performance_work.constraint: Already isolated from the HTTP event loop and scoring process. Further cache or materialization must invalidate on production, reference and filter changes; stale exports are unacceptable.

remaining_performance_work.item: Profile the endpoint or query associated with a sustained latency alert before changing worker count, SQL indexes or database topology.
remaining_performance_work.constraint: Avoid trading CPU saturation, SQLite contention or memory pressure for apparent parallelism.

safety_and_scope: No production sheet was edited or validated to manufacture monitoring evidence.
Validated records and concurrent-write protection remain intact.
No OCR provider or model switch was required for these review flow fixes.
Optional plan comparisons may still show differences, but they do not veto a human save or validation.

validation.event_loop_regression: A deliberately blocked database write does not block a concurrent health request.
validation.timing_limitation: One synthetic browser flow against a disposable local database; not production user measurements.

prior_latency_work: docs/ocr-latency-2026-10-15.json preserves measurements and runtime hashes for the preceding performance release. Current human-review changes supersede overlapping files.

historical_write_observations.note: Internal validation durations omit HTTP queueing and other work. Legacy logs cannot distinguish older synthetic requests. Historical requests are not proof of post-publication performance.

final_read_only_public_checks.note: No synthetic POST or production validation was performed.

final_read_only_public_browser.note: Production read-only check: no values were filled or submitted; all non-read requests were blocked.
